roundNote: Round 8 tests the answer to review round 6. 650e3cb5 merges main forward and brings Dispatch's 0141. b5d974fd adds one identifier rule both runners load (packages/envoy/migrationid, Check) and records no last number. 9ce23f73 makes autodeploy.sh's rollback guard and the loadtest seed check compare the set of applied migrations, and updates the docs. Dispatch's createVersionTable is unchanged since round 7, so round 7's rolling-deploy proofs still apply.

implementerProof.how: The proofs the implementer records hold where I drove them: 0141 is byte-identical to main; the identifier, pgmigrate, migrationid and migrate tests pass at this head on my own PostgreSQL 18.6; autodeploy.sh's guard and the loadtest seed check do what the handoff says on real psql output. The implementer's proof does not cover the case below. The handoff's own description, 'no last number', is the cause.

failures.criterion: Migration identifiers two concurrent pull requests cannot both claim, for both runners (plan.md 'Migration numbering' item 1, from the INFRA-537 spec v2)
failures.evidence: migrationid.Check (b5d974fd) accepts any numbered series 1..N with no gap. Nothing records where the numbered migrations ended, so a branch that adds the next number is a valid longer series. Driven in a scratch clone: branches nbx and nby off 9ce23f73 each add packages/daemon/internal/store/migrations/0062_t588_<x|y>.up.sql and packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/migrations/0142_t588_<x|y>.up.sql + .census.sql. On each branch alone, the daemon's migrations package tests and Dispatch's TestMigrationSetTakesNumbersThenTimestamps pass ('ok'). git merge-tree of the two gives exit 0, tree 42acee2d. Only the merged tree fails: 'migrations 0062_t588_x.up.sql and 0062_t588_y.up.sql share version 62' and 'migrations 0142_t588_x.up.sql and 0142_t588_y.up.sql share version 142'. That is the conflict the change exists to remove: both pull requests pass, and the second to merge must renumber. Negative control, the previous round's code 7ab3f40f, which recorded the last number: a branch adding the daemon's 0062 alone fails 'migration 0062_t588_x.up.sql takes version 62: a migration added after 0061 is named for the UTC moment it was created', and Dispatch's 0141 alone fails '140 is the last numbered migration'. Review round 6 asked to set the last number to 141 (finding 1); this head removed it instead. Red tests, each its own commit: packages/daemon/internal/store/migrations/next_number_test.go TestLoadRefusesANewMigrationNumberedAfterTheShippedSet (7feb642d6bbb) and packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/next_number_test.go TestMigrationSetRefusesANewMigrationNumberedAfterTheShippedSet (a25cec37291a). Each adds a file numbered one past the shipped set's highest numbered migration and expects the refusal to name it. Commands: cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/store/migrations/ -run '^TestLoadRefusesANewMigrationNumberedAfterTheShippedSet$' -count=1, which fails 'Load accepted the shipped set plus 0062_next_number.up.sql'; cd packages/envoy && go test ./internal/dispatch/store/ -run '^TestMigrationSetRefusesANewMigrationNumberedAfterTheShippedSet$' -count=1, which fails 'the identifier check accepted the shipped set plus 0142_next_number.up.sql'. The daemon test passes when copied onto 7ab3f40f. The Dispatch test reads the set as TestMigrationSetTakesNumbersThenTimestamps does, through migrationid.Check(versions). If the fix moves that check to another entry point, tell me and I will move my test to it, since the test is not the implementer's to change.

proof.criterion: A failed deploy that applied a migration below the highest applied version is not rolled back onto the previous image (review round 6, finding 2)
proof.surface: autodeploy.sh's schema_applied, schema_max, schema_label and roll_back_or_stop, extracted as written, against real psql output from PostgreSQL 18.6; only docker is stubbed (pg_client runs the script's own psql line locally; compose and rollback log)
proof.command: database ad with schema_migrations holding 1..141 and 20261029210000; baseline=$(schema_applied); then roll_back_or_stop sha-new sha-prev <baseline> 8766 after: (1) nothing applied; (2) 20261029200000 inserted, below the max; (3) the same with a legacy bare-max baseline; (4) a legacy baseline with the max raised; (5) an unreachable database
proof.observed: baseline 20261029210000-142-656ea3c9…; (1) 'rolling back to sha-prev (schema 20261029210000 (142 applied))', exit 0; (2) 'refusing to roll back to sha-prev … changed the applied migrations to 20261029210000 (143 applied)', exit 1; (3) rolls back, the documented comparison for a baseline the previous deployer wrote, which can meet no timestamped migration since pre-change images carry none; (4) refused, exit 1; (5) 'could not read the schema version … (status 2), so refusing', exit 1
proof.negativeControl: the previous deployer's schema_version and roll_back_or_stop (650e3cb5) on case (2): 'rolling back to sha-prev (schema 20261029210000)', exit 0, onto a schema the previous image never ran on

proof.criterion: The loadtest seed check compares the set of migrations, not the highest (review round 6, finding 4)
proof.surface: loadtest/common.sh's build_migration_versions and seed_migration_check, extracted as written, with die and note stubbed; the seed's migrations list from stack.sh's own query on PostgreSQL 18.6
proof.command: seed.meta.json with migrations [..141, 20261029200000, 20261029210000] from "select coalesce(json_agg(version order by version), '[]'::json) from schema_migrations"; build directories copied from this head's Dispatch migrations plus T1+T2 (both), T2 only, or T1+T2+T3 (extra); then the same with a legacy meta holding only .migration
proof.observed: both: nothing printed; T2 only (same max as the seed): 'DIE: the seed holds 1 migration(s) this build does not have, the highest 20261029200000'; extra: 'NOTE: this build holds 1 migration(s) the seed lacks, the highest 20261029220000'; legacy meta: 'NOTE: this seed records only its highest migration … only the highest is compared'
proof.negativeControl: the previous check compared the highest file name only (removed lines of 9ce23f73): T2 only reads as build_level 20261029210000 = seed_level, so it passes
